crop.notes: Whole column item with main headline 'Tom Allen as a Boxer' and subheads.

ocr.notes: Main headline missing; 'Telegraph to the Express' should be 'to the Record'; Allen (not Fox) failed to appear at the Police Gazette office and went to Coney Island 'for a plunge in the surf'; Harding 'did not go to the theatre'; Hill would not allow articles signed in his house; last line is Sullivan's match with Mr. Elliott, not Allen, postponed; several sentences paraphrased.

summary.suggested: The Wilkes-Barre Record reported that Tom Allen's poor showing as a boxer at Madison Square Garden left friends urging backer Richard K. Fox to drop his $5,000 offer to match Allen against John L. Sullivan.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Wilkes-Barre Record, Friday Morning, December 1, 1882; dispatch dated New York, Nov. 30. article.json has no focus field.

facts.fact: Allen gave an unsatisfactory boxing exhibition in the art gallery of Madison Square Garden, New York, on a Monday evening
Richard K. Fox of the Police Gazette proposed to wager $5,000 that Allen could defeat John L. Sullivan in the prize ring and posted $1,000 with Harry Hill
After the exhibition Fox tried to withdraw the $1,000, while Sullivan's friend Robert Farrell claimed it for Sullivan; Hill refused to give it up until Fox's man declared Allen would not fight

notes: Exhibition date inferred: 'Monday evening' before the Nov. 30 dispatch is Nov. 27, 1882.
